problem: The figure rewrites the target (∂S/∂V) at constant T as the Jacobian ratio J(S,V)/J(T,V). That ratio is not the target: with the held-constant variable T, the correct ratio is J(S,T)/J(V,T). As printed, a student would copy the wrong ratio into the worked example and get −(∂S/∂T)V instead of (∂P/∂T)V, and the stated result of the figure would not follow.
fix: Change the 'jac' node note to 'J(S,T) / J(V,T)', matching step 1 of the worked example and the identity (∂u/∂x)y = J(u,y)/J(x,y).

where: exam traps, second trap (sign of a swap)
problem: 'Reversing the order and keeping the sign flips the answer' is ambiguous: reversing the order is exactly what flips the sign, so 'keeping the sign' after a reversal is the mistake that makes the answer wrong. A student can read it either way.
fix: Write: 'J(u, v) = −J(v, u). If you swap the order of the two functions you must also change the sign; swapping the order and forgetting the minus sign gives an answer with the wrong sign.'

problem: 'the determinant of their first derivatives' is loose; the Jacobian is the determinant of the 2×2 matrix of first partial derivatives, which is what the formula that follows actually shows.
fix: Say: 'the Jacobian of two functions u(x, y) and v(x, y) is the determinant of the 2×2 matrix of their first partial derivatives.'
